title: Panther Tracks
tools: Microsoft Word, OneDrive, Adobe Illustrator, Canon EOS 6D, Countless Notebooks
summary: Writing, photography, and production for Seattle Prep’s annual alumni and community magazine.
paragraphs: In mid-2023, I worked on my first issue of Panther Tracks — Seattle Prep’s annual community and alumni magazine. Since then, I’ve contributed to four issues. From writing alumni features, student profiles, institutional triumphs each year to capturing, organizing, and identifying the right imagery that effectively told Seattle Prep’s story. It truly became a labor of love.

Diving headfirst into production when I first began at Seattle Prep, two things happened. One, I strengthened my skills as a writer. Until this point, I typically wrote in academic contexts. Now, my sentences would grace the mailboxes and coffee tables of over 10,000 alumni, donors, and families. Slightly frightened at that thought, I was also energized to tell the stories of Seattle Prep with accuracy and meaning.
Read my favorite pieces from our most recent issue here!

title: Alumni Week Branding
summary: A refreshed Alumni Week identity brought to life across print, web, and digital communications.
paragraphs: Engaging alumni is paramount to a healthy and robust school community. To that end, I made a consistent effort to build relationships with alumni. Be that the Gen Z recent grads to the Baby Boomers that saw the Seattle tech boom take place.
Using insights gained from connections, I aided the Assistant Director of Alumni Engagement in revamping Seattle Prep’s Alumni Week.

Flexing my graphic design skills, we collaborated to develop a fresh brand identity to promote various events and opportunities to reconnect alumni with Seattle Prep. Through Direct Mail postcards, an updated website, and digital collateral, we’ve achieved a refreshed Alumni Base that get excited for our events.

title: Admissions Communications and Marketing
role: Graphic Design, Writing, Email Marketing, Photography, Video Production, Project/Vendor Management
tools: Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Premiere Pro, Canon EOS 6D, Canon R6 Mark II, iPhone, CapCut, Finalsite Messages, MailChimp, Veracross
summary: Integrated admissions campaigns, print design, storytelling, and video built around THINK PREP.
paragraphs: Seattle’s is home to a competitive independent school market. Thus, a major factor in my work is crafting campaign strategies and tactics that allow our admissions office to stand out and spark curiosity among prospective families and students.

Seattle Prep’s current campaign encourages those families and students to consider why the school’s approach to education rooted in the Jesuit paradigm is worth our tuition in the age of AI — THINK PREP!

My work with admissions spans from inquiry to enrollment. Designing postcards, posters, and brochures for Open House, ideating and executing long and short-form video projects that highlight the school’s differentiators, and composing email campaigns that reassure the decision to enroll.

title: Social Media Strategy
role: Content Creation, Photography, Content Planning and Management, Graphic Design
tools: Sprout Social, Canon EOS 6D, iPhone, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Lightroom
summary: Platform-specific content strategy, community storytelling, and performance-informed social media management.
paragraphs: Social media is the modern search engine, primary sources at your fingertips. I managed Seattle Prep’s official social channels with an emphasis on content strategy, community-centered storytelling, audience growth, and performance-informed planning.

In creating authentic, platform-specific content, data analysis, and content planning through Sprout Social for the schools Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn accounts. Through strategic and consistent posting, Instagram engagement has boosted 408%

title: Prep Post — A Weekly Newsletter
role: Content and Submission Management, Editorial Direction, Photography, Writing, Graphic Design
tools: Finalsite Messages, Canon EOS 6D, Countless Notebooks
summary: Editorial planning, writing, and production of Seattle Prep’s weekly community newsletter.
paragraphs: At 7, my first email account was with Yahoo Mail. I remember the excitement in receiving mail in the almost archaic platform from my favorite cousin, Paty, who had just moved to Utah.
Believe it or not, I still carry that child-like excitement for email.

Every Monday during the academic year, I produce Seattle Prep’s weekly newsletter, Prep Post. My process, more so a ritual, grants me the chance to connect with the entire school community. Faculty and staff alert me of noteworthy material, and I synthesize the past week and week ahead in a reliable and readable digital news resource.
Since Prep Post fell under my direction, I’ve maintained an 80% percent open rate on average, with click-through rates varying dependent on content of the week.
